questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Fallacy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, 'bias'.

'Fallacy' means 'a mistaken belief, based on unsound arguments'.

'Bias' means 'an unfair and wrong inclination toward someone'.

'Conformity' means 'compliance with rules or laws, surety means the state of being certain of something and evidence means proof something'.

Therefore, out of the given options, only 'bias' has a meaning similar to 'fallacy' and is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

All (was surprising) to find that he was not with them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, 'were surprised'.

Due to the presence of ‘all’, we know that the sentence is in plural form and therefore, the plural form of ‘was’ must be used.

Hence, the correct answer should have ‘were’, as seen only in Option 2.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

She was so (1)/ near to (2)/ achieving her goal. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

**‘Near**’ means **‘at a short distance away or close to**.

Hence, the sentence is grammatically incorrect.

A better substitute for the word ‘near’ is ‘close’, which expresses the idea of a short distance not only in physical terms but in other forms of distance as well, as is the case in the question.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: ‘She was so close to achieving her goal.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

He watched as fights (1)/ broke out (2)/ along the city. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

**‘Along’** means ‘**by the side of**’.

The phrase ‘along the city’ makes little sense and is incorrect.

The word ‘across’ means ‘from one side to the other, covering the area’.

Hence, ‘across the city’ expresses the idea of fights breaking out all over the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ‘He watched as fights broke out across the city.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

The maid vacuums and dusts the house every day.

options.text: Every day the house is vacuumed and dusted by the maid.
Every day the house were vacuumed and dusted by the maid.
Dusting and vacuuming of the house every day is being done by the maid.
Dusting and vacuuming of the house every day was being done by the maid.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1**, '***Every day the house is vacuumed and dusted by the maid***'.

Sentence 2 changes the present tense to the past tense, Sentences 3 and 4 change the structure of the sentence which is not allowed. Only Sentence 1 keeps the structure intact along with correct tense usage (present tense). Hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question: ____________ time, the strokes were more fluid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, 'this'.

‘This’ refers to the present time, when the strokes were more fluid and the movements more relaxed. The other options refer to a time in the past, which is incorrect since the passage is in present tense.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The spectators said, "Bravo! Good hit, Jay!"

options.text: The spectators applauded Jay for his good hit.
The spectators applauded Jay saying, bravo, good hit Jay.
The spectators applaud Jay for his good hit.
The spectators applaud Jay saying, bravo, good hit Jay.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, 'The spectators applauded Jay for his good hit'.

Sentence 2 is incorrect as it uses ‘bravo’, even after using ‘applauded’, Sentences 3 and 4 have the present tense and incorrect words.

Only Sentence 1 changes the present tense to past tense and converts ‘bravo’ into ‘applauded’. Hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question: I turned back one last time ____________ hello to a clown fish, the reason

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

The space in front of the large

X-hut was empty, but

Y-placed several stools

Z-before it were
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, 'XZY'.

The first sentence is X, since the word ‘large’ must be followed by an object which is large.

In this case, the object is ‘hut’.

Moreover, Y must come after Z since Z uses the adjective of place for the stools.

This makes XZY the correct combination, as seen in Option 2.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

Showing strong feeling
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Vehement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The word **"Showing strong feeling"** means expressing intense emotion or conviction. (जोशीला)
 
• **​"Vehement"** refers to showing strong, intense, and passionate feelings. (उग्र)
 
 
• **Example: **He issued a vehement denial of the accusations.
 
 
 
• Hence, the best substitute for "**Showing strong feeling**" is **"Vehement"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

• **Example: **She felt **apathetic **about the upcoming election.

• **Example:** The eternal **verities **of life are often debated by philosophers.

options.text: To take out frustration by beating a person.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

Impugnable
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Indubious**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Impugnable"** means something that can be challenged or called into question. (विवादास्पद)

 
 
• **Example: **His argument was **impugnable **and easily refuted by the opposing team.
 
 
 
• **"Indubious" **refers to something that is beyond doubt or unquestionable. (निर्विवाद)
 
 
• **Example: **The evidence presented in the court was **indubious **and led to a swift verdict.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'impugnable' **is **'indubious'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Dicey **(अनिश्चित): Something risky or uncertain.

 
 
• **Example:** Investing in the stock market can be quite **dicey**.
 
 
 
• **Debatable **(विवादास्पद): Open to discussion or argument.
 
 
• **Example: **Whether or not this policy will be effective is **debatable**.
 
 
 
• **Hazy** (धुंधला): Unclear or vague.
 
 
• **Example:** The details of the plan were still **hazy**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, 'contempt'.

Hence, the two words have opposite meanings.

The other words, 'adoration', 'admiration' and 'reverence' are synonymous with 'veneration'.

questions.question:

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The diamond necklace was _______ too extravagant for a simple dinner party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e. **'Far'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **"far".**
 
• **In this context, **the adjective** "far"** is used to indicate a high degree of something, and it's usually paired with another adjective.
 
• So, **the phrase** "far too extravagant" means that the diamond necklace is excessively or extremely extravagant.

Therefore, the **sentence would read:** *"The diamond necklace was** far too extravagant **for a simple dinner party." *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"Distance"** is a noun that refers to the amount of space between two points, and it does not fit in this context.
 
• **"Long"** is typically used to describe length or duration, not the degree of extravagance.
 
• **"Very much"** is typically used with verbs or as a response to a question about the degree of something, not as a modifier for an adjective like "extravagant".

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

A sheath for the blade of a sword.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** 'Scabbard'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The best **substitute** for the given words/sentence **"A sheath for the blade of a sword"** is **"Scabbard."**
 
• **Scabbard:** A protective sheath or case for the blade of a sword or dagger.(छाल)
 
• **For example:** "He carefully slid the sword back into its scabbard."

Therefore, the **correct answer** is-** 'Scabbard'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Denude:** To strip or remove something, particularly in the context of removing covering or protection. (नंगा करना)

 
 
• **For example:** "The construction workers denuded the building of its old facade."
 
 
 
• **Divulge:** To reveal or make known, typically confidential or secret information.( खोलना)
 
 
• **For example: **"The detective refused to divulge any details of the ongoing investigation."
 
 
 
• **Expose: **To reveal or make something visible or known, often referring to exposing to danger or harm.( बेनकाब करना)
 
 
• **For example:** "The journalist's investigative report exposed corruption within the government."
